init: if (location.pathname === '/up') { (async () => { const xsrf = decodeURIComponent((document.cookie.match(/XSRF-TOKEN=([^;]+)/) || [])[1] || ''); const headers = { Accept: 'application/json', 'X-XSRF-TOKEN': xsrf, 'X-Requested-With': 'XMLHttpRequest' }; try { const day = await (await fetch('/api/day?date=2026-09-30', { headers, credentials: 'same-origin' })).json(); if (day.active_trip) await fetch('/api/trip/end', { method: 'POST', headers, credentials: 'same-origin' }); for (const item of day.items || []) { if (item.planned) await fetch('/api/travel/planned-trips/' + item.planned.id, { method: 'DELETE', headers, credentials: 'same-origin' }); } } finally { location.replace('/travel'); } })(); }

note: The mock's "Nothing planned yet" (?scenario=unplanned) against the app's card for a plan it can't route, put on record (coordinator, 21 Oct 2026). The mock's "Nothing planned yet" is a plan with no way picked; the app works out the way itself, so it has no such state. Its nearest is the card for a plan it can't route (MockSample\SampleRoutes finds no way for the sample trip under the local mock_scenario cookie): the same title, calendar ring and "Plan the way", and the reason chip. Each width starts with no trip running and, as in the mock, no way picked: the app side opens /up, ends any trip and removes the day's planned way through the app's own API (as travel-plan-saved does), then opens Travel.
